finding.title: Fix the tautological awk comparison in make audit check 15 so cross-feature deep imports are ever reported
finding.why: awk's match() finds the leftmost occurrence of `features/([^/]+)/` in $0, which for a `file:line:content` grep line is always inside the FILE PATH itself (it precedes the content). So a[1] (from $1, the path) and b[1] (from $0) are always derived from the same leading match and are always equal — `a[1] != b[1]` can never be true. I reproduced this directly: piping the real repo through the exact pipeline yields 0 lines even though 1186 lines match the pre-filter pattern, and manually evaluating the awk on a scheduler_providers.dart import line prints `a=scheduler b=scheduler` for an import that is unambiguously FROM `features/learning/`. Rule 2 is marked [E] (enforced) but its checker is structurally incapable of ever printing a violation or failing, regardless of how much cross-feature coupling exists — `make audit PASSED` gives false assurance for this rule specifically (distinct from the already-documented 'warn-only' gap, which assumed the check merely doesn't fail the build, not that it is inert).
finding.recommendation: Rewrite the check-15 pipeline to compare the importing file's own feature (parsed once from $1) against the imported feature (parsed from the import statement/content portion only, e.g. by stripping $1 and the line number before matching), and add a fixture test (a temp file with a deliberate deep cross-feature import) asserting the check's exit/output actually flags it before merging any fix.
acceptance_criteria: `make audit` check 15 prints at least one file:line when a deliberate cross-feature deep import is introduced in a throwaway test fixture.
A regression test or CI fixture pins this behavior so the check cannot silently regress to a no-op again.
